heroHeadline: Legislature approves 90-day extension of state of exception 100-58 over COB and FENCOMIN objections, as Senate opens a special commission into the Cerimedo corruption case
heroSubtitle: The Plurinational Legislative Assembly's overnight session approved Decree 5707's 90-day extension of the state of exception in force since June 20, passing 100-58 (122 deputies and 36 senators participating) after running past 1 a.m. on Sept. 17. COB executive secretary Mario Argollo and FENCOMIN president Josué Caricari both rejected the extension as legally unjustified given no active blockades and each announced an undated national assembly to plan a response, while protesters gathered peacefully near Plaza Murillo with no clashes reported. Separately, the Senate activated a six-member, three-party special commission on Sept. 18 to investigate corruption allegations tied to detained presidential adviser Fernando Cerimedo, the same day Nadia Beller testified roughly three hours to prosecutors, requested protected-witness status citing safety fears, and said the Aug. 17 attack on her was meant to silence a corruption denunciation. The floated boliviano eased further to Bs. 9.83/$1 on Sept. 17 before ticking back up to Bs. 10.01/$1 on Sept. 18.
